result.summary:
Read lib/letflow/design/req060-pin-rebind.md in full (566 lines) against REQ-060's six ACs (docs/requirements.yaml:3266-3272). All six map to named design elements: AC1->S4 M5/M6+S5 payload shape; AC2->S4 M4 (all-or-nothing pass, no partial writes before Multi); AC3->S4 M2's own eligibility predicate (explicitly NOT InstanceProjection.terminal?/1, correctly, since terminal?/1 excludes :error per instance_projection.ex:178-179); AC4->S4 M0.3/M0.4/M0.5 (reason/entries/malformed-entry, each a distinct error atom or tagged tuple); AC5->S7 (zero PinResolver/Reconstruction code changes needed, since merge_effective_pins/2 and reconstruct_effective_pins/2 already do the work); AC6->S4 M1 (NOWAIT) + S6 (lock scope) + S2 moduledoc item 3 (ERROR-is-terminal statement). No TBD/deferral language found. Ran grep -nE '^\s*(def|defp|with .* <-|case .* do$)' myself against the file directly: zero matches -- the doc is call-order prose (named function, input, {:ok,...}/error contract) plus @type/@spec blocks only, no real .ex bodies.

Independently verified both confirmed-not-assumed claims against shipped code, not the doc's citations: (a) grep -n 'FOR UPDATE\|NOWAIT' across lib/letflow/engine/reconstruction.ex and lib/letflow/engine.ex confirms reconstruction.ex:710 (lock_projection_nowait/2) is the only 'FOR UPDATE NOWAIT' in the codebase, and engine.ex:2002/2015/2061 (cancel_instance/3's locks) are all plain 'FOR UPDATE' -- exactly as claimed. instance_projection.ex:178-179 confirms terminal?/1 excludes :error. (b) Read pin_resolver.ex:433-465 directly: merge_effective_pins/2 folds ALL pins_rebound_events via Enum.reduce (not just latest), and apply_rebind_event/2 reads payload['entries']||payload[:entries], with each entry read via entry['kind']||entry[:kind] etc -- exactly the shape section 5's payload produces, confirming REQ-060 needs zero PinResolver/Reconstruction changes. tenant_provisioning.ex:515-524 confirms only INSTANCE_STARTED is auto-seeded.

Resolved section 9's five OQs: OQ-1 (self-registration) -- correct as designed; rebind_pins/3 must NOT self-register INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND, matching the TASK_COMPLETED/INSTANCE_CANCELLED precedent (registry.ex:169-180's get_type/2 fails closed regardless of writer; provisioning only ever seeds INSTANCE_STARTED per its own 'No other event type is seeded here' comment, tenant_provisioning.ex:515-516) -- self-registering here would be the outlier, not the norm. OQ-2 (missing vs empty reason) -- one :invalid_reason atom is correct; REQ-060 AC4's text lists 'a missing or empty reason' as one single tested scenario, not two, so a single atom is not an ambiguity, it is the literal AC reading. OQ-3 (zero-changed-entries rebind) -- 'always append, possibly empty entries' is the correct and only defensible reading: AC1's text is 'an entry whose requested version already matches contributes no payload entry' -- scoped to the entry, not the whole call; nothing in AC1-AC6 states the whole rebind is skipped when all entries are no-ops, and a rebind that resolved every ref successfully but changed nothing is still a distinct, auditable outcome from one that failed at M2/M4 -- collapsing it into 'no event' would make a successful no-op indistinguishable from validation never having run. OQ-4 (ConcurrentModification scope) -- rebind-vs-any-lock-holder (the design's stated reading) is correct, not rebind-vs-rebind-only: AC6's text says 'lock contention surfaces as a distinct ConcurrentModification error rather than blocking' with no scope qualifier, and the design's own instance_projections NOWAIT lock is the same row cancel_instance/3/complete_task/3 already lock via plain FOR UPDATE (engine.ex:2002/2015/2061) -- a narrower scope would require a second, rebind-specific lock target with no requirement text asking for one. OQ-5 (no R-Co source) -- non-blocking documentation caveat only, correctly flagged as such, does not affect any AC's testability.

All five OQs resolve to the design's own stated reading being correct -- none required a design change, so no rework needed. Section 10's AC-to-design-element self-check table verified accurate against the actual mapping I derived independently above.
result.next_action: Route to next WF-02 step (ELIXIR-DEV implementation) -- design gate cleared. REVIEWER should still see OQ-1/OQ-3/OQ-4 readings noted above during code review since they are judgment calls the requirement text does not spell out character-for-character, even though this validation found none of them ambiguous enough to block.
